summary.headline: Q2 FY27 turnover rose 41.2% YoY to INR2,914 crores, revenue up 30% to INR44.58 crores, PBT up 9.6% to INR5.33 crores.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 as a record quarter, with turnover of about INR2,914 crores (up 41.2% YoY) and revenue of INR44.58 crores (up 30% YoY). PBT rose 9.6% YoY to INR5.33 crores, and H1 PBT was INR5.91 crores, with Q2 contributing about 90% of it. Growth was driven by outward remittance (Q2 up 53.9% YoY) and student and B2B business, with commission payouts raised, which compressed margins. The expanded AD-II mandate (perpetual licence from July 30) opens forex correspondent (FXC) and trade remittance routes, both guided to go live in Q3 to Q4.

financial_highlights.change: +17.6% YoY (as stated in one section); CFO later said ~18%
Management said higher payout reflects wallet-share strategy; no confirmation of figures

segments.name: Student
segments.commentary: Turnover up 44.2% YoY; still the largest segment, supported by about 90 new student partners in H1 and NBFC partnerships. Management said the overall US student market dipped while UK and Australia grew.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Turnover up 12.3% YoY in Q2; management said corporate is at about 40-50% of pre-COVID levels. Active corporates stood at 944.

segments.name: Retail / D2C
segments.commentary: Growth of 19.1% YoY, with a 25.51% CAGR cited; management is deliberately pacing D2C because acquisition cost is high, and is leaning on partners and branches.

segments.name: Cards
segments.commentary: Card business CAGR of 62.08%; the company moved from bank-partner programmes to its own GlobalPay card, with 30 currency wallets and 22 regulated-entity card distribution partners onboarded.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 numerical guidance given; management said it cannot speculate but is positive on H2 given new trade and FXC activation.
Forex correspondent (FXC) rollout: board-approved policies in place, expected to roll out by November 2026.
FEDAI membership in progress; trade remittance expected to go live around December 2026 to January 2027 (later stated as Q4), with SOPs to be drawn once membership is granted.
Trade transactions permitted up to INR25 lakhs per transaction; management cites trade TAM rising from USD20 billion to USD200 billion.

Management expects FXC distribution to reduce yield (revenue sharing with partners) but save on fixed costs, enabling asset-light reach expansion; a few new branches may be added in the next 3-6 months.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 26; Thane and Whitefield branches added in the quarter; couple more branches possible in next 3-6 months.
Forex correspondent network to be operational around Q3; trade-related activity to be operationalised in Q4.
Nostro account activated and partnership signed with Mastercard Move; card distribution went live in Q2.
Digital penetration around 70%, target 90%; CKYC 2.0 integration being pursued for end-to-end digital onboarding.
Own tech team builds solutions; card development platform built in-house; CDP (card) platform and partner integrations ongoing.
demand_pricing: Management said the overall market dipped due to forex volatility, US visa uncertainty, Middle East conflict and weak discretionary travel; April was a big dip.
Two months in Q2 crossed INR1,000 crores monthly turnover.
Q2 is seasonally the strongest quarter; Q1 weakest; Q3 and Q4 taper but stay better than Q1.
Commission payouts raised to win wallet share; management said payouts depend on partner business potential rather than a flat rate.
Management said travel-led retail is hurt by cheaper credit card and currency substitutes; D2C acquisition cost is high.

qa_highlights.question: Has commission to agents risen from 52% to 58%, and is 58-60% the new norm?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher payout is the strategy to increase wallet share; payouts vary by partner, so there is no flat norm.

qa_highlights.question: Trade payments scope, and whether a PA-CB licence is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RBI asked the company to work with FEDAI; SOPs follow membership, expected in November. It will first operationalise AD-II and consider PA-CB later.

qa_highlights.question: Commission as a percentage of turnover versus EBITDA margin decline (15-16% to 12%)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said incremental business came from B2B channels with higher commission. Commission was about 88-89 bps of turnover in the prior-year quarter, which included a one-time visa incentive; the amount was to be provided by email.

qa_highlights.question: Will FXC and distribution lift profits from INR7 crores to INR20 crores in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numerical target; it said reach and trade could grow revenue without corresponding costs but yield would dip due to partner sharing.

qa_highlights.question: Treasury income and customer float on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the float reflects customer funds received before remittances and card settlements complete, and treasury income should rise with card volumes. No quantum was given.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from higher partner commission payouts and revenue sharing with FXC and card distribution partners; EBITDA margin cited by analyst fell to about 12% from 15-16%.
Dependence on US student and visa flows; management said US dipped and UK and Australia grew.
Regulatory execution risk on FEDAI membership, SOPs and trade remittance go-live timelines, which keep slipping.
Customer float and card settlement liabilities rising; the company did not quantify the split between remittance and card balances.
Retail and D2C remain soft; management is cautious on cash burn for performance marketing.
Q2 seasonality: H1 PBT is concentrated in Q2, so H2 earnings need to be tracked closely.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and expanded licence scope, but cautious and evasive on numbers: no FY27 guidance, the commission-margin question and the one-time visa incentive were deferred to email, and several questions were answered with qualitative positioning.
key_quotes: So, this has been a record Q2 for us with a turnover of around INR2,914 crores, 41.2% growth year-on-year.
This is about expansion without asset-light expansion. So, without corresponding cost, we can increase our reach.
Segment is not growing. In fact, US has dipped.
We are not going, as I always say, that we don't go all out on D2C because we feel that business has to be done prudently and keeping a margin.

adds.what: Thane and Whitefield branches added in Q2; a couple more branches possible in next 3-6 months
Forex correspondent (FXC) network rollout, board-approved, expected by November 2026 (around Q3)
Trade remittance route, pending FEDAI membership, expected Dec 2026 to Jan 2027 (later stated as Q4)

growth.why: No FY27 numerical guidance; management is positive on H2 with FXC (guided by November) and trade remittance (Dec-Jan, Q4) as new routes, while Q2 revenue rose 30% YoY and turnover 41.2% YoY, backed by branch additions and partner-led growth but without quantified targets.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 PBT of INR5.91 crores is concentrated in Q2 (about 90%), Q1 PBT was only INR0.58 crores, and the Q3-Q4 seasonal taper plus the margin squeeze from partner payouts could weigh on H2 earnings.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The FXC network is expected by November 2026 (Q3), trade remittance under AD-II is guided for December 2026 to January 2027 (Q4), and the GlobalPay card with 30 currency wallets and 22 card distribution partners is already live.

rows.label: Commission payout pressure and FXC revenue sharing reducing yield
rows.why: Management said higher payouts are the wallet-share strategy and FXC distribution will reduce yield through partner revenue sharing, while the analyst cited commission rising from 52% to 58% (unconfirmed).
